newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK-Stocks continue strong rise.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK-Stocks continue strong rise.

text.p: The Botswana stock market continued to perform strongly in the week ending May 30 as both domestic and overseas demand drove share prices higher.
The domestic companies index gained 11.5 points to close at 483.37 points, leaving shares 37 percent higher in pula terms and 41 percent higher in US dollar terms than at the start of the year.
A number of shares showed significant increases and volum over the week.

There was Foreign interest in varable loan stock counter RDC Properties as a block of 605,522 changing hands at 180 thebe and 178 thebe. RDCP listed just over 500,000 new units as a result of its capitalisation issue on Wednesday.

Botswana Insurance put on 10 thebe to 260 thebe, Security group Inco put on 20 thebe on the back of its interim results. Brewery holding company Sechaba also put on 20 thebe to 395 thebe on the back of both domestic and and overseas institutional buying.

Barclays continued to rise and ended the week up 5 thebe at 760 thebe. Clothing chain Pep traded up 5 thebe to 310 thebe. Foreign buying drove milling company and food wholesaler Sefalana up 35 thebe to 490 thebe.
Trading unchanged were: Food and tobacco wholesaler Metsef at 660 thebe, First National FNBB.BT at 520 thebe, investment counter Kgola ya Sechaba at 190 thebe and Standard Chartered at 630 thebe.
Domestic volume traded was significantly up at 1,016,460 from last week's 204,424.

On the the foreign board, trade was down, with only 100 car rental and fleet management group Avis AVIS.BT shares changing hands. The counter closed 31 thebe down at 623 thebe. Unchanged and untraded were: De Beers at 12,719 thebe, McCarthy Retail MCTJ.BT group at 1,100 thebe and Regent undervalued asets fund REAF.BT at 4,000 thebe.
The foreign index shed 0.34 points to 390.87.
The All Companies Index barely moved, losing 0.02 points to 393.25.
